Pile
pyle
n. (a heap, especially of wood for burning)
Latin pila, a pillar or pier. The Authorized Version uses the noun twice, and in both it means a pyre — the heaped wood of a burning, in Isaiah for Tophet and in Ezekiel for the bloody city.

Biblical Definition

Isaiah ends his oracle against Assyria with the furnace prepared for its king: “For Tophet is ordained of old; yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made it deep and large: the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it” (Isaiah 30:33). Tophet was the valley where Israel had burned its own children to Molech; the prophet turns the place of Judah's worst sin into the figure of God's judgment on the tyrant. Two details govern the verse: the pile was ordained of old, prepared long before the king who would need it, and it is kindled not by human hands but by the breath of the LORD. Ezekiel uses the same image against Jerusalem herself: “Woe to the bloody city! I will even make the pile for fire great” (Ezekiel 24:9). God builds no pile for an enemy he will not also build for a guilty city bearing his own name.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines pile as a heap; a mass or collection of things thrown together in a heap; and specifically, a heap of combustibles for burning a body.

expand to see more

PILE, n. A heap; a mass or collection of things in a roundish or elevated form.

PILE, n. A collection of combustibles for burning a dead body; a funeral pile.

PILE, n. A large stake or piece of timber, pointed and driven into the earth, as for the support of a building.

TOPHET, n. In Scripture, a place near Jerusalem in the valley of Hinnom, where children were sacrificed to Moloch.

BRIMSTONE, n. Sulphur; a hard, brittle, inflammable substance, of a lemon yellow color.

Key Scripture

Isaiah 30:33 — "For Tophet is ordained of old; yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made it deep and large: the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it."

Ezekiel 24:9 — "Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Woe to the bloody city! I will even make the pile for fire great."

Isaiah 30:27 — "Behold, the name of the LORD cometh from far, burning with his anger, and the burden thereof is heavy: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire:"

Ezekiel 24:6 — "Wherefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Woe to the bloody city, to the pot whose scum is therein, and whose scum is not gone out of it! bring it out piece by piece; let no lot fall upon it."

Modern Corruption

Divine judgment is widely treated as sub-Christian and unworthy of God, where the prophets describe a pile ordained of old and kindled by God's own breath, and aim the same fire at Jerusalem as at Assyria.

expand to see more

It is now common to hear that the wrath in passages like Isaiah 30:33 belongs to a primitive stratum of religion which the gospel has outgrown, and that a God of love could not be described kindling a pyre. Two features of the text make that reading impossible. First, the pile is ordained of old — not an outburst of temper but a settled purpose, older than the offender. Second, Ezekiel aims the identical image at Jerusalem, the city of God's own covenant, and calls her the bloody city. A judgment that falls hardest on the household of God is not tribal favouritism; it is holiness, and the New Testament says judgment must begin at the house of God.

The place Isaiah chose carries the argument further. Tophet was where Judah had burned her sons and daughters in the fire to Molech, and God takes the scene of the nation's deepest abomination as the figure of his own righteous burning. The principle to recover is that God's wrath is not the opposite of his love but its defence: a God who would not prepare a pile for tyrants and for bloody cities is a God indifferent to the children in the valley. And the gospel does not remove the fire; it tells us who bore it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew medurah (H4071), a pile or pyre; Topheth (H8613), Tophet; gophriyth (H1614), brimstone; neshamah (H5397), breath.

expand to see more

Hebrew medurah (H4071) — a pile of fuel, a pyre; the pile of Isaiah 30:33 and Ezekiel 24:9.

Hebrew Topheth (H8613) — Tophet, the place of burning in the valley of Hinnom.

Hebrew gophriyth (H1614) — brimstone, sulphur; the stream that kindles the pile.

Hebrew neshamah (H5397) — breath; the breath of the LORD doth kindle it.

Hebrew ir haddamim — the city of bloods; Ezekiel's name for Jerusalem under judgment.

Usage

"“Tophet is ordained of old” — a settled purpose, not a temper."

"“The breath of the LORD... doth kindle it” — no human hand."

"“Woe to the bloody city! I will even make the pile for fire great”."
